newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares jump to closing AEX high of 594.33.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares jump to closing AEX high of 594.33.

text.p: Dutch shares closed at a record high on Friday, powered by brisk options-related business as derivatives traders closed positions for the monthly exipirations, squeezing shares higher in the cash market.

"If you look at it, it really is quite narrowly based with a couple of stocks going up a lot and the rest not doing that much," said one trader. Dealers said investors covering AEX index puts at 595 got the upper hand over players holding AEX index options expiring at 590.
The cash index closed 4.59 points up at 594.33, comfortably past the October 15 closing high of 592.45.
Heavy options business in the hours before the close pushed the AEX up to its highest ever level -- 596.08 -- above the previous all-time high of 594.73 set on October 15.
Dealers said the market could be set for a small consolidation in the next few weeks before pressing on again for a year-end target of 600.

One said recent profit warnings from Philips and Toolex this week had prompted some concern that further bad news could be on the horizon and that could trigger consolidation. "I think there's a chance we might see some more of that sort of thing and that won't really help things much near term."
Dealers said the market was monitoring the political situation in Russia after Thursday's surprise sacking of security chief Alexander Lebed by president Boris Yeltsin.
"I think everybody is still thinking about Russia and that might put a brake on any further gains," a third dealer said. "There's some nervousness about Russia of course," said another.

Chemicals company Akzo surged 8.80 guilders to 221.80, just back from a year's high of 222.00. One market-maker said he had heard a U.K. based brokerage had executed a buy programme in the stock after issuing a buy recommendation. "We've seen a persistent buyer in the stock for the past few days," he said.
